text.p: British food and drinks giant Grand Metropolitan Plc posted a six percent rise in its full year pretax profits on Thursday to 965 million pounds ($1.59 billion) and chairman George Bull said trading in the current year had started "satisfactorily."

Profits grew 30 percent at its North American foods business Pillsbury to 431 million with both sales and prices up and its spirits arm International Distillers and Vitners posted a four percent increase in trading profit to 471 million.

"Pillsbury continues to outperform the U.S. food industry and deliver strong, profitable growth. IDV showed progress on all fronts, with volume increases accompanied by price rises and improved profitability," said Bull.

But operating profits from its fast food chain Burger King fell 29 million to 167 million pounds ($275.9 million) in the year ended September 30, 1996 hit by difficult trading in Britain and Germany due to the beef crisis and the slowing pace of refranchising outlets. The company opened 756 restaurants in the year to bring its worldwide total to 8,696.

IDV profits were driven by spirits sales up five percent and average price rises of two percent. The results also benefited from an increased investment in marketing up 25 million to 427 million, said GrandMet. The company's top five brands are J&B, Smirnoff, Bailey's, Malibu and Jose Cuervo. Pillsbury included a full year from Pet, producer of Old El Paso and Italian foods and soups, which was acquired in February 1995. It cashed in on rising U.S. raw material costs by putting through price rises on all its major brands like Haagen-Dazs ice cream, Green Giant and Pillsbury. ($1=.6054 Pound)
